# pgwerk

pgwerk is a Postgres-backed job queue library for Python. It stores jobs as database rows and dequeues them with SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Workers also use LISTEN/NOTIFY to wake up immediately on enqueue instead of polling on a fixed interval.

## Key facts

- Install: pip install pgwerk
- Requires: Python 3.11+, Postgres 14+, psycopg3
- License: MIT
- Source: https://github.com/pgwerk/pgwerk
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/pgwerk/

## What it does

- Background job execution with four worker types: AsyncWorker (asyncio), ThreadWorker, ProcessWorker, ForkWorker
- Transactional enqueue — jobs can be enqueued inside a Postgres transaction; rollback cancels the job
- Retry with configurable back-off intervals
- Delayed jobs and cron scheduling (Scheduler, requires pip install pgwerk[cron])
- DAG-style job dependencies
- Idempotency keys and concurrency groups
- Built-in dashboard and CLI

## Limitations

- Not suitable for very high throughput (millions of jobs per second) — Postgres lock contention becomes the bottleneck
- Python-only protocol, no cross-language workers
- Requires Python 3.11+ and psycopg3; no support for other database drivers
- Newer and less battle-tested than Celery or RQ
